bindingContractTests.case: Tenochtitlan conquest boundary accepts prior observation
Tenochtitlan rejects modern Mexico City record
Cairo accepts only 1000 in Modelski ancient series
Cairo rejects 900 in Modelski ancient series
Constantinople rejects Ottoman-only dated capital claim

Unknown record never matches by name or proximity

coordinateReview: Existing source coordinates were inspected; no coordinates or historical polygons were added. Matching tests validate identity/date rules, not archaeological boundary accuracy.
sourceAccessException: rome-colosseum was read in the web search index of the official page; direct open returned an internal error. All other cited pages opened successfully.

manualReview.identity: Roma / Rome records are explicitly named; the Pleiades urban point and the later capital/population points lie in the same historic city.
manualReview.time: The Pleiades record stops at 640; it does not support all later years. Later exact-ID observations/claims remain separate. The dossier does not assign a factual 753 BCE foundation date.

manualReview.identity: Use Constantinopolis, the dated Constantinople claims, and explicitly time-filtered Istanbul population observations.
manualReview.time: Dossier scope 330–1453. Byzantium pleiades:520985, modern İstanbul pleiades:77402394 and the Ottoman-only capital claim are excluded. The text explicitly includes the interruption of Byzantine rule in 1204–1261; broad capital claims are preserved as source claims, not used to erase that interval.

manualReview.identity: A dossier about al-Qahira from 969, not an assertion that the earlier Fustat, al-Askar and al-Qatai settlements bore that identity.
manualReview.time: Pre-969 observations are excluded. Commissioning al-Azhar in 970 and beginning citadel work in 1176 are deliberately distinguished from completion. The city reference point is not relabelled as a palace, mosque, or the medieval centre.

manualReview.identity: chandler:1433 is named Tombouctou and is the exact bound record.
manualReview.time: Population evidence covers the listed observations 1300–1850. The fourteenth-century manuscript node is a century range, not a precise event on 1 January 1300. The 1733 node is the copying date of a surviving manuscript, not the date the astronomical ideas originated.

manualReview.identity: There is no independently named Tenochtitlan record in the current place data. Only the pre-conquest 1500/1520 observations in chandler:921 (Mexico City) are bound.
manualReview.time: Scope 1325–1521. The 1325 foundation is identified as traditional. No Modelski 2000 or post-1521 Chandler observations may match.
manualReview.space: The source point is an urban reference near the ancient city, not an archaeological fix on the Templo Mayor, and no ancient-city polygon is supplied. It is preserved unchanged. Modern Mexico City extent and Xochimilco are not substituted for the island city.

manualReview.identity: chandler:346 is named Cuzco; Q5582862 was separately checked on Wikidata as the historic city of Cusco, not inferred from proximity alone.
manualReview.time: The 1438 expansion and 1533 Spanish arrival have institutional sources. Source observations 1438–1850 remain discrete.
manualReview.space: The source coordinate is a city reference point, not a precise Qorikancha or royal-plaza location. The article describes the historic city without relocating the dataset point.

editorialExclusions: No population figure was added from museum/UNESCO narrative sources; divergent historical population estimates remain in the underlying observation datasets.
No comprehensive city-boundary reconstruction or coordinate-accuracy upgrade is implied by these reading dossiers.
No current opening hours, visitor arrangements, state-of-conservation claims or changing political status were added.
No paragraph repeats generic non-representation disclaimers; identity and spatial qualifications live in scope/binding metadata.
No source photographs, maps, or prose were copied. Source title and URL metadata are retained for citations.
The UNESCO Cairo synthesis contains an apparent east/west reversal for the Nile and Muqattam; that orientation claim is not used.
INAH main-domain pages returned errors on direct opening; the cited INAH Lugares historic-centre page opened successfully and supports the retained Tenochtitlan claims.
integrationRequirements: Use exact sourceRecordIds. Never use a fuzzy city-name match or a distance threshold to attach dossiers.
Pass the selected observation year when binding population records; all such bindings require an observation and an allowed observationYears value.
Intersect dated-place matches with the source periods. Do not interpolate across period gaps.
Display milestone labels/date objects; do not format decade/century start years as falsely exact single-year events.
Keep scope/binding explanations in the sources or dossier-information panel; prose is intended for direct reading.
The Tenochtitlan dossier must be hidden from modern Mexico City and post-conquest source observations.
